;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[November 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
***A [[car bombing]] leaves at least four soldiers dead and five others injured in [[Paghman District]], [[Kabul Province]]. [https://tolonews.com/afghanistan-167728 (TOLOnews)]
*[[Kashmir conflict]]
**[[2020 India–Pakistan border skirmishes]]
***Cross-border shelling between [[India]]n and [[Pakistan]]i troops kill 15 people, including ten civilians, and five security personnel. The [[Indian Army]] says it foiled an "infiltration attempt from Pakistan" in northern [[Kashmir]] whereas the [[Pakistan Army]] claims it responded to "unprovoked and indiscriminate firing" from India. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-india-pakistan/indian-and-pakistani-troops-exchange-fire-at-least-15-dead-idUKKBN27T22H?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Tigray military intervention]]
**The [[United Nations]] says that [[war crimes]] might have been committed in the [[Tigray Region]] of [[Ethiopia]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/war-crimes-feared-ethiopia-s-tigray-conflict-thousands-flee-neighboring-n1247664 (NBC News)]
*Aftermath of the [[1998 United States embassy bombings]]
**An intelligence official says that [[Abdullah Ahmed Abdullah]], [[Al-Qaeda]]’s second-in-command, accused of helping to mastermind the 1998 bombings of two United States embassies in Africa, was killed in [[Iran]] in August by Israeli operatives. [https://www.smh.com.au/world/middle-east/israeli-operatives-killed-al-qaeda-s-no-2-20201114-p56eml.html (''The New York Times'' via ''The Sydney Morning Herald'')]
*[[2020 Western Saharan clashes]]
**[[Polisario Front]] declares war on [[Morocco]] accusing Rabat of breaking the 1991 ceasefire. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-11-13/morocco-moves-army-to-end-western-sahara-blockade-le360-reports (Bloomberg)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Pacific typhoon season]]
**The death toll from the [[landfall]] of [[Typhoon Vamco (2020)|Typhoon Vamco]] in the [[Philippines]] rises to 53, according to the [[Philippine National Police|national police]], with at least 22 still missing. The provinces of [[Cagayan]] and [[Isabela (province)|Isabela]] in [[northern Luzon]] are the most affected, mainly caused by [[floodwater]]s from the [[Magat Dam]]. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-11/14/c_139515539.htm (Xinhua)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Illinois]]
*****[[Illinois]] registers 15,415 new cases in the last 24 hours, a new single-day record, breaking a national record that was previously set by [[Florida]] on July 12, when that state reported 15,299 cases. [https://chicago.cbslocal.com/2020/11/13/covid-19-in-illinois-state-shatters-case-record-with-15415-new-infections-hospitalizations-and-testing-also-reach-new-highs/ (WBBM-TV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Maryland]]
*****[[Maryland]] reports 1,869 new cases, a new single-day record. [https://www.baltimoresun.com/coronavirus/bs-md-coronavirus-cases-maryland-november-surge-hogan-20201113-i5ro6xg2cnfztlj4zpoiyjnslq-story.html (''The Baltimore Sun'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan]]
*****[[Michigan]] reports 8,516 new cases, a new single-day record. [https://www.clickondetroit.com/health/2020/11/13/michigan-coronavirus-cases-up-to-244741-death-toll-now-at-7929/ (WDIV-TV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nevada]]
*****[[Nevada]] [[Governor of Nevada|Governor]] [[Steve Sisolak]] tests positive for [[COVID-19]]. He says he is symptom-free but will quarantine at his home for ten days. [https://www.reviewjournal.com/news/politics-and-government/nevada/gov-sisolak-tests-positive-for-covid-19-2182941/ (''Las Vegas Review-Journal'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)|COVID-19 pandemic in New York]]
*****[[New York (state)|New York]] reports more than 5,000 new cases for the first time since April, when the state registers 5,401 cases. The positivity rate also reaches 2.65 percent. [https://thehill.com/homenews/state-watch/525908-new-york-tops-5000-covid-cases-for-the-first-time-since-april (''The Hill'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in North Dakota]]
*****[[Governor of North Dakota|North Dakota Governor]] [[Doug Burgum]] issues a statewide [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|face mask mandate]] and impose several business restrictions in an effort to contain the spread of COVID-19. The new executive order will take effect tomorrow. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/north-dakota-orders-mask-mandate-business-restrictions-74204949 (ABC News)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oregon]]
*****[[Governor of Oregon|Oregon Governor]] [[Kate Brown]] announces a statewide two-week "freeze" starting November 18, which will limit restaurants and bars to take-out only and close gyms, indoor and outdoor recreational facilities. [https://www.opb.org/article/2020/11/13/oregon-governor-kate-brown-covid-19-restrictions/ (OPB)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.]]
*****More than 130 [[United States Secret Service|Secret Service]] agents have been ordered to isolate or quarantine because they tested positive for the coronavirus or had close contact with infected co-workers. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/secret-service-coronavirus-outbreak/2020/11/13/610eebcc-2539-11eb-8672-c281c7a2c96e_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Wisconsin]]
*****[[Wisconsin]] reports 7,777 new cases, a new single-day record. The state also surpasses 300,000 total confirmed cases. [https://www.wbay.com/2020/11/13/new-coronavirus-record-puts-wisconsin-over-300000-cases/ (WBAY-TV)]
****Nationwide, more than 180,000 cases reported in the [[United States]], a new world record. [https://www.forbes.com/sites/tommybeer/2020/11/14/another-grim-new-record-us-tops-180000-new-infections-friday-covid-cases-rising-in-all-50-states/ (''Forbes'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in British Columbia]]
*****[[British Columbia]] reports a record of 617 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing its total number of cases to 20,985. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/covid-19-cases-bc-nov-14-2020-1.5801263 (CBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Delhi]]
*****[[Delhi]] reports 104 new fatalities on Thursday, the highest single-day figure since the beginning of the pandemic, bringing the overall death toll to 7,332. [https://www.newindianexpress.com/cities/delhi/2020/nov/13/covid-19-death-count-in-delhi-crosses100-for-first-time-2223051.html (''The New Indian Express'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]], [[COVID-19 vaccine]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record 5,444 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total to 457,735 cases. [[Central Java]] reports the highest number of new cases, with 1,362 new cases. [https://health.detik.com/berita-detikhealth/d-5253836/rekor-5444-kasus-baru-13-november-berapa-spesimen-covid-19-yang-diperiksa (detikHealth)]
****[[President of Indonesia|President]] [[Joko Widodo]] states that the country has sought emergency authorization to start a mass [[vaccination]] programme by the end of the year using [[CoronaVac]] and the [[China National Pharmaceutical Group|Sinopharm vaccine]]. He also said that health workers, [[Indonesian National Armed Forces|military]] and [[Indonesian National Police|police]] will be the first to receive the vaccine. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-indonesia-president-e-idUSKBN27T11A (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] begins to fine people and operators who fail to wear masks in public. Under the new rules, people caught without masks in public venues face fines of up to 100,000 [[South Korean won|won]] (US$90), while the operators of those places face fines of up to three million won (US$2,700). [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2020/11/13/asia-pacific/south-korea-fining-masks/ (''The Japan Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****The number of new confirmed cases in [[Germany]] surges to a record 23,542 cases over the past 24 hours, according to data from the [[Robert Koch Institute]]. [https://www.zeit.de/wissen/gesundheit/2020-11/coronavirus-neuinfektionen-rki-gesundheitsaemter-bayern-baden-wuerttemberg (''Zeit Online'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****The number of new confirmed cases in [[Italy]] surges to a record of 40,902 cases, pushing the nationwide total to 1.1 million cases as the [[Government of Italy|government]] designates the [[Tuscany]] and [[Campania]] regions as high-risk "red zones". [https://www.ansa.it/english/news/general_news/2020/11/13/covid-40902-new-cases-550-victims_83442d74-16e4-4746-8ee5-f4165ae7fa75.html (ANSA)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-54937699 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Portugal]] surpasses 200,000 cumulative cases of COVID-19. [https://covid19.min-saude.pt/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/256_DGS_boletim_20201113.pdf (DGS)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
** After a series of briefings against [[Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] and his wife, two of his Special Advisers [[Dominic Cummings]] and [[Lee Cain]] (also [[Downing Street Director of Communications]] left their roles in [[Number 10 Downing Street]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record 21,983 new cases in the past 24 hours, pushing the nationwide total since the start of the pandemic to 1.88 million cases. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2020/11/13/russia-nears-22k-coronavirus-infections-in-new-daily-record-a72038 (''The Moscow Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden]]
****[[Sweden]], whose government took a lighter approach to the pandemic, including not enforcing [[lockdown]]s, reports 5,990 new cases, a new single-day record that pushes the nationwide total to 177,395 cases. [https://m.dagensvimmerby.se/nyheter/e/79909/coronaviruset-13-november-manga-nya-dodsfall-i-sverige-ett-i-kalmar-lan/ (Dagensvimmerby)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland]]; [[COVID-19 vaccine]]
****[[Switzerland]] begins reviews of [[Moderna]]'s potential vaccine candidate. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-moderna-swiss-idUSKBN27T1LS (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****The number of new confirmed cases in [[Ukraine]] surges to a record of 11,787 cases, pushing the nationwide total since the start of the pandemic to 512,652 cases. [https://www.kyivpost.com/ukraine-politics/covid-19-in-ukraine-11787-new-cases-172-new-deaths-269486-active-cases.html?cn-reloaded=1 (''Kyiv Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[Prime Minister of Australia|Prime Minister]] [[Scott Morrison]] announces that all [[States and territories of Australia|states and territories]] in [[Australia]] will reopen their borders by [[Christmas]], with the exception of [[Western Australia]]. [https://www.9news.com.au/national/coronavirus-national-cabinet-scott-morrison-state-borders-reopen-christmas/f023ed4a-fed6-4120-9461-498ed7afe37e (9 News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
****The [[Auckland CBD]] reopens after contact tracing of a new case revealed it was linked to a known case from a border isolation facility, reversing an earlier call for people to work from home. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/430533/no-new-community-cases-auckland-cbd-to-reopen (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic on cruise ships]]
***Seven passengers on [[SeaDream Yacht Club]]'s ''[[SeaDream I]]'' cruise ship test positive for COVID-19, forcing the cruise line to cancel the remainder of the sailing and return the ship to a port in [[Barbados]]. [https://www.cnn.com/travel/article/caribbean-cruise-seadream-1-covid/index.html (CNN)]

;Law and crime
*[[Corruption in South Africa]]
**[[Ace Magashule]], a top official of the [[African National Congress]], is expected to face 21 charges of corruption in [[Bloemfontein]], [[South Africa]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/south-african-ruling-party-official-charged-corruption-74190534 (ABC News)]
*[[Terrorism in Germany]]
**[[Public Prosecutor General (Germany)|Federal prosecutors]] in [[Stuttgart]] [[Landesgericht (Germany)|state court]] charge 11 people with membership of the "{{interlanguage link|Group S.|de|Gruppe S.}}" [[Right-wing terrorism|far-right terror]] organization, allegedly planning to effect "conditions similar to civil war" by killing Muslims and attacking mosques so as to "shake the [[State (polity)|state]] and the [[social order]]" and eventually overthrow the German government. [https://www.dailyherald.com/article/20201113/news/311139968 (AP via ''Chicago Daily Herald'')]
*[[Alcohol in Indonesia]]
**Twenty-one lawmakers from staunchly conservative Islamic parties, the [[Prosperous Justice Party]] (PKS) and the [[United Development Party|Development Unity Party]] (PPP), re-initiate their argument at the parliament to have the Bill on the Prohibition of Alcoholic Drinks passed into law. The bill has stalled in parliament ever since it was initiated by the same group in 2015. [https://coconuts.co/bali/news/bali-officials-voice-concerns-over-deliberations-on-alcohol-ban/ (Coconuts)]
*A major police operation is conducted at the headquarters of [[Ubisoft Montreal]] following reports of a hostage situation. The employees remaining in the building are safely evacuated. Later, the [[Service de police de la Ville de Montréal|police]] tell the local media that it was a false alarm. Police sources deem the 911 call that triggered the incident a hoax. [https://www.journaldemontreal.com/2020/11/13/possible-prise-dotages-chez-ubisoft-a-montreal (''Le Journal de Montréal'')] [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/montreal-police-ubisoft-1.5801236 (CBC)]
*Recently unsealed court documents reveal that a teenager had been arrested last year for plotting an attack on an unidentified school in the [[Tasman District]] of [[New Zealand]]. He was in possession of an [[AR-15 style rifle]], a modified shotgun, and homemade explosives. The suspect had pleaded guilty to charges of unlawful possession of restricted weapons and objectionable material and had been sentenced to two years of supervision. [https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/300158323/teen-planned-mass-shooting-at-new-zealand-school (''Stuff'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Belarusian protests]]
**Protesters gather in [[Belarus]] to mourn the death of 31-year-old protester Raman Bandarenka, who died in a hospital in [[Minsk]] after being beaten by security forces. [https://abcnews.go.com/amp/International/wireStory/eu-decries-belarus-violence-opposition-supporter-death-74187198 (ABC News)]
*[[2020 Myanmar general election]]
**Early results show [[Myanmar]]'s ruling [[National League for Democracy]] winning an absolute majority in the country's latest general election. The election is called unfair by the oppositional [[Union Solidarity and Development Party]] and is criticised by rights groups for alleged [[voter suppression]] and the political disenfranchisement of the [[Rohingya people|Rohingya minority]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/myanmar-election-aung-san-suu-kyis-party-wins-absolute-majority/a-55584326 (DW)]

;Sports
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]]
**The [[Egyptian Football Association]] announces that [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] forward [[Mohamed Salah]] has tested positive for COVID-19 shortly before Egypt's [[2021 Africa Cup of Nations qualification|2021 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier]] match against [[Togo national football team|Togo]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/11/13/liverpool-football-star-mohamed-salah-tests-positive-for-covid-19 (Al Jazeera)]
